headline_findings: Per-stream professional edge is small: the median/average GROSS Sharpe of a single-market, single-engine trend stream run by professionals is ~0.3-0.4 (Trends Everywhere median 0.34-0.35 across 82+ assets 1985-2017; AQR Century paper ~0.4 avg per market; Rob Carver (ex-AHL) budgets 0.40 pre-cost for a single instrument with diversified rules). A shop's headline Sharpe of 1.5-2 is NOT built from per-stream Sharpes of 1.5-2.

Breadth is the dominant Sharpe factory: with average pairwise correlation rho between streams, portfolio Sharpe = stream Sharpe x sqrt(N/(1+(N-1)rho)), asymptoting at stream Sharpe/sqrt(rho). Measured rho between per-market trend streams is 0.04-0.07 (0.17 within equity factors), giving a 3-4.5x aggregation multiplier: 0.34 per stream -> 1.17 (traditional assets), 1.34 (alternative assets), 1.60 gross combining all groups (Babu-Levine-Ooi-Pedersen-Stamelos, JOIM 2020). The arithmetic reproduces the observed portfolio Sharpe almost exactly (0.34 x sqrt(50/(1+49x0.07)) = 1.14 vs observed 1.17). This is Grinold's fundamental law (IR = IC x sqrt(breadth), JPM 1989) operating in futures form.

Style stacking adds a second breadth axis: carry per asset class averages Sharpe 0.78 (equities 0.91, FX 0.68, commodities 0.60, FI slope 1.03, credit 0.47) and the diversified Global Carry Factor reaches 1.20 (Koijen-Moskowitz-Pedersen-Vrugt, JFE 2018, Table 2); carry, trend, value, defensive are imperfectly correlated, so multi-style futures books stack another ~1.2-1.5x. Note the same paper's honest caveat: 9 asset classes should give 3x if independent; observed gain was only ~60% (cross-asset carry correlation is real).

Realized index-level truth for diversified trend at industry scale: SG Trend Index Sharpe ~0.61 since Jan 2000, CAGR ~5.2%; BTOP50 CAGR ~3.9-4.1% at ~9.6% vol. The AQR century backtest (1903-2012, 59 markets) delivered Sharpe 1.00 NET of simulated 2/20 fees and t-costs at 9.9% vol (gross 20.0%/yr, net 14.3%/yr). So live-index diversified trend earns 0.5-0.6 net, best-practice backtests 1.0-1.2 gross-of-fee-equivalent -- all from per-market streams of ~0.35.

Multi-manager platforms industrialize the same math: Millennium runs 330+ independent pods (~$70-80B) and has returned ~14% annualized since 1989 with one down year (2008); Citadel Wellington 19.2% net annualized since 1990, $90.4B lifetime net gains (LCH Investments) -- these are hundreds-to-thousands of tightly risk-capped, netted streams plus leverage, not one big edge. Platform-level Sharpe figures of ~2.5-2.6 circulate but are UNVERIFIED (no audited public source).

Vol targeting is a real but second-order and fragile Sharpe source: Moreira-Muir (JF 2017) find inverse-variance scaling of the market earns 4.9% annualized alpha, appraisal ratio 0.33, ~25% Sharpe improvement (in-sample); Cederburg-O'Doherty-Wang-Yan (JFE 2020, 103 strategies) show real-time implementable versions generally earn LOWER Sharpe than the unmanaged portfolio; Harvey et al. (JPM 2018, 60 assets since 1926) find Sharpe gains only for risk assets (equity/credit), negligible for bonds/FX/commodities, but universal left-tail reduction. Its main production role is keeping risk constant so breadth and leverage work, not raising Sharpe per se.

Execution/cost edge preserves, rather than creates, Sharpe: on $1.7T of live institutional trades across 21 markets, realized costs are an order of magnitude below academic estimates (~10-20 bps), and break-even capacities are large (combined value+momentum ~$98B; 4-strategy combo ~$51B at 3%/yr net) (Frazzini-Israel-Moskowitz, Trading Costs 2018; Trading Costs of Asset Pricing Anomalies). Cost engineering is what lets a 0.3-per-stream edge survive multiplication by 100 streams.

Capacity and Sharpe trade off at the extremes: Medallion averaged ~66% gross/yr for 30 years (SD ~31.7%, Sharpe >2, reported peaks much higher) only by capping capacity near $10B and using ~12.5x average leverage on high-frequency-ish, short-horizon signals (Zuckerman 2019; Cornell 2020). Conversely, futures TSMOM shows little evidence of binding capacity (demanded contracts < open interest 1986-2011, Baltas-Kosowski), which is why diversified CTAs run $100B+ at Sharpe ~0.6.

The 'many persistently profitable intraday traders' premise has a measured base rate: in the complete Taiwan Stock Exchange record 1992-2006 (~450,000 day traders/yr), fewer than 1% predictably and reliably earned positive abnormal returns net of fees; the top-500 (top ~0.1%) earned 37.9 bps/day after fees (Barber-Lee-Liu-Odean, JFM 2014). Persistent solo intraday profitability exists but is a <1% tail, and even winners' edges are execution-intensive and small per trade.

Honest decomposition for a reported Sharpe 1.5-2 systematic non-HFT shop: per-stream net edge ~0.2-0.4 (that is ~15-25% of the headline number); breadth x low correlation (50-500 market-engine streams at rho 0.05-0.2) contributes a 3-5x multiplier (~60-75% of the headline); style stacking and netting another ~1.2-1.5x; vol targeting +0-25% on risk-asset sleeves (in-sample-fragile); execution/cost engineering protects ~0.1-0.3 Sharpe that naive implementation would burn. No public evidence exists of professionals sustaining Sharpe 1.5-2 from ONE market with ONE engine class at meaningful capacity, other than capacity-capped short-horizon shops (Medallion-type), which is a different business.

winners.bottom_line: The owner's intuition ('so many people run persistent-Sharpe systematic strategies, we cannot be stuck') is correct about the industry but wrong about the mechanism. Persistently profitable systematic non-HFT managers do not own per-stream edges materially better than yours: the professional norm for a single-market, single-engine stream is gross Sharpe ~0.3-0.4 (Trends Everywhere median 0.34; AQR century avg ~0.4; Carver's 0.40 budget), and even the flagship diversified products realize only ~0.6 net at industry scale (SG Trend since 2000). Headline Sharpes of 1.5-2 are manufactured almost entirely by aggregation: 50-500 near-uncorrelated streams (markets x engines x styles) at pairwise rho ~0.05-0.2 give a 3-5x sqrt-N multiplier (~60-75% of the headline), style stacking (trend+carry+value+defensive) another ~1.2-1.5x, with vol targeting (+0-25%, risk assets only, fragile out-of-sample per Cederburg et al.) and cost engineering (preserving ~0.1-0.3 Sharpe; real costs ~10-20 bps per FIM) as second-order terms. The only documented route to Sharpe >2 without breadth is capacity-capped short-horizon trading (Medallion: ~$10B cap, 12.5x leverage, effectively a different business), and the solo-intraday-winner base rate is <1% of the population (Barber et al. 2014). Implication for this program: a dev Sharpe ~1.26 on ONE market with one engine family is already at or above the per-stream quality of professional books; by the industry's own production function, the next unit of portfolio Sharpe is far more likely to come from adding genuinely decorrelated return streams (other markets, other engine classes, other holding horizons/styles on the same infrastructure) than from further tuning NQ intraday engines -- the program is not 'stuck', it is at the breadth-1 frontier where every professional shop would also plateau.

headline_findings: BASE RATE (futures day trading, Brazil): Of 19,646 individuals who began day trading mini-Ibovespa futures 2013-2015, only 3.0% of the 1,551 who persisted 300+ sessions had ANY positive lifetime net profit (97% lost). Only 1.1% (17 people) out-earned Brazil's minimum wage (~US$16/day) and 0.5% (8 people) out-earned a starting bank teller (US$54/day). Top survivor: US$310/day mean with US$2,560 daily SD. Profitability share declines MONOTONICALLY with experience (29.8% profitable among 1-day dabblers down to 3.0% among 300+ day persisters) and fixed-effects regressions show no learning-by-trading. Verified verbatim from the working-paper PDF.

BASE RATE (stocks, Taiwan, full-market data 1992-2006): ~450,000 individuals day trade in an average year (17% of TSE volume). ~20% of substantive day traders show positive net abnormal returns in any given year, but only ~4,000 (<1% of the population) PREDICTABLY profit net of costs year-over-year. Aggregate day traders lose 7 bps/day gross and 23.9 bps/day net (costs triple the loss); >75% quit within two years. Verified from published JFM 2014 paper and the RAPS 2020 companion.

THE PERSISTENT MINORITY IS REAL AND ITS SKILL IS LARGE: Taiwan's prior-year top-500 day traders go on to earn 61.3 bps/day gross, 37.9 bps/day NET the following year, with a mean daily Sharpe (net daily return / daily SD) of 0.66 during ranking. The top ~6,000 (of 450k) earn reliably positive net alphas. So persistent intraday alpha exists at the extreme tail — it is not folklore — but the base rate is <1%, not 'many'.

WHAT THE WINNERS DEMONSTRABLY DO (evidence, Taiwan): (1) past performance is by a large margin the best predictor of future performance; (2) second-best predictor is CONCENTRATION of trading in a few stocks — specialization for informational advantage; (3) their profits concentrate in hard-to-value stocks (small, volatile) and around earnings announcements — i.e., forecasting short-horizon moves under information asymmetry; (4) short-selling usage proxies sophistication. Explicitly REJECTED as the main driver: passive liquidity provision — even the most profitable group takes liquidity on ~2/3 of trades and order aggressiveness barely predicts future profit.

WHAT OTHER DOCUMENTED WINNERS DID (US, structural rents): Harris & Schultz (JFE 1998) SOES bandits earned small per-trade profits by picking off slow-updating NASDAQ dealer quotes; Garvey & Murphy's 15 zero-commission proprietary traders (96,323 trades, 2000) profited primarily via Island ECN limit orders placed inside dealer quotes, trading mornings/high-volume/high-volatility when uninformed liquidity flow was present, and updated quotes faster than market makers. These are market-structure/fee-structure edges tied to a now-extinct regime (pre-decimalization, pre-HFT), not generic chart-reading.

FOLKLORE VS EVIDENCE: no peer-reviewed evidence that retail DOM/order-flow 'tape reading' per se generates persistence; the documented mechanisms are specialization + information-asymmetry timing + execution/fee advantages. Chague et al. additionally present suggestive evidence that rising HFT activity is a headwind to retail day-trader P&L.

REGULATOR DISCLOSURES (leveraged retail intraday-style products): ESMA (27 Mar 2018, ESMA71-98-128): national regulators' analyses show 74-89% of retail CFD accounts lose money, average losses (euro)1,600-(euro)29,000 per client. FCA CP16/40 (Dec 2016): 82% of sampled UK CFD clients lost, average -(pound)2,200/client/year, and EXPERIENCED clients lost more than inexperienced. AMF France (Oct 2014): 89% of 14,799 active CFD/FX clients lost over 2009-2013; losers lost (euro)175M total vs (euro)13.8M won by the 1,575 winners. CNMV Spain: 82% of CFD clients lost Jan 2015-Sep 2016 ((euro)142M).

PROP-FIRM / FUNDED-ACCOUNT FUNNEL: no major firm (incl. FTMO) publishes audited pass/payout rates — circulating '7-10% pass FTMO' figures are untraceable (UNVERIFIED). Best available industry dataset (FPFX Technologies via Finance Magnates, Sept 2024; 300k+ accounts, ~100k traders, 10 firms): ~14% pass evaluations, ~45% of funded accounts ever receive a payout (~7% of all buyers), average payout ~4% of nominal account size (~$4,000 on $100k) vs ~$800 average challenge spend across ~3 attempts. CFTC's 2023 My Forex Funds fraud complaint (135k customers, $310M+ fees) was DISMISSED in May 2025 with sanctions against the CFTC — treat its allegations as unproven.

IMPLICATION FOR THE OWNER'S CHALLENGE: the premise 'many intraday traders are persistently profitable' overstates the honest base rate by roughly two orders of magnitude (0.5-3% of persisters, <1% predictable). Simultaneously, the tail's measured economics (37.9 bps/day net for a year ahead, out of sample) prove markets DO permit persistent intraday alpha — but the documented route is narrow specialization, information-asymmetry timing, and cost/structural advantage, not breadth of strategy search. A single-market portfolio at dev Sharpe ~1.26 is already tail-consistent, not evidence of being 'stuck'.

daytraders.bottom_line: The owner's premise fails on base rates but succeeds on existence. Honest numbers: among people who actually persist at day trading, only ~3% show any lifetime net profit (Brazil futures, 300+ sessions) and ~0.5% earn a modest living wage; in the only full-market long-horizon dataset (Taiwan, 15 years), <1% of ~450,000 annual day traders are PREDICTABLY profitable net of costs, and regulator disclosures (ESMA 74-89%, FCA 82%, AMF 89%) plus prop-firm funnel data (~7% of challenge buyers ever see a payout, averaging ~$4k) confirm the same shape everywhere. So 'many intraday traders are persistently profitable' is survivorship folklore — the true persistent minority is on the order of 1-in-100 to 1-in-200 of those who try seriously. However, that minority is real and its edge is enormous (37.9 bps/day net, out-of-sample, for the top 500), which proves markets do leave persistent intraday alpha on the table. The documented paths to it are: extreme specialization/concentration in a few instruments to build an informational edge, timing short-horizon moves where information asymmetry is highest (news/earnings, volatile hard-to-value names, when uninformed flow is present), and cost/market-structure advantages (fee structures, execution rents) — NOT passive liquidity provision, NOT generic pattern breadth, and NOT (per any published evidence) retail DOM-reading. For this program: being 'stuck' at portfolio Sharpe ~1.26 on one market is already consistent with the documented right tail; the literature's implied search direction is deeper specialization and information-asymmetry/timing concentration plus cost engineering, not a wider trawl of generic signal families.

edges.name: Overnight drift concentrated at European open (2:00-3:00am ET, equity index futures)
edges.mechanism: Inventory risk: liquidity providers absorb end-of-US-day order imbalances and unwind into the European open; the drift is compensation for holding inventory overnight. Payers = impatient close-of-day flow (institutional rebalancers). Persisted because overnight liquidity provision was capacity-constrained.
key_citations: Boyarchenko, Larsen, Whelan, 'The Overnight Drift', Review of Financial Studies 36(9):3502-3547, 2023 (also NY Fed Staff Report 917)
NY Fed Liberty Street Economics, 'The Disappearing Overnight Drift', July 2026
edges.effect_size: ~3.7%/yr earned in the 2-3am ET hour alone, >60% of the ES contract's 5.9% annualized close-to-close return, sample 1998-2020; highly significant in-sample.
edges.power_on_20y_nq: N≈5,000 nights. Per-night effect ≈1.5 bps in a 1h window with sd ≈25 bps ⇒ t ≈ (0.000147/0.0025)·√5000 ≈ 4.2 at published size — detectable on 20y. But NY Fed 2026 update: Jan 2021-Dec 2025 returns in that window ≈ 0; end-of-day order-imbalance dispersion compressed >50% (RSV sd 6.5%→2.9%), removing the inventory-risk compensation.
edges.notes: The cleanest documented single-index-futures OHLCV edge in the mandate list, and it is now formally documented as dead post-2021 by the original authors' institution. A 20y backtest will 'find' it (pre-2021 subsample) and live trading will not collect it. Any test must be regime-split at ~2021.

Payers = hedgers paying the basis.

edges.mechanism: Volatility is persistent but expected returns do not rise one-for-one with vol (esp. after vol spikes), so cutting exposure when vol is high raises Sharpe. Persists because it requires uncomfortable procyclical de-risking and leverage in calm markets.
